root_cause.text: An off-by-one indexing error in the second `memcpy` of the `lowpan_iphc_mcast_ctx_addr_compress` function in `net/6lowpan/iphc.c` causes the group ID to be copied to incorrect offsets, leaving the last byte of an uninitialized stack buffer (`data`) unwritten and subsequently leaked over the network.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that the second `memcpy` was corrected from `memcpy(&data[1], &ipaddr->s6_addr[11], 4);` to `memcpy(&data[2], &ipaddr->s6_addr[12], 4);`, and the `data` array was changed from `u8 data[6];` to `u8 data[6] = {};` to prevent transmitting uninitialized stack memory.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix 6LoWPAN multicast address compression offsets and initialize the temporary buffer to prevent stack data leakage.
intent_record.what: Initializes the 6-byte data array to zero and adjusts the destination offset from index 1 to 2, and the source offset from index 11 to 12, for copying the 4-byte multicast group ID.
intent_record.how: Ensures that the destination buffer is fully initialized to prevent memory leaks and corrects the byte alignment of the compressed multicast address fields during 6LoWPAN header compression.

The 'data' buffer is allocated on the stack without initialization, which allows the unwritten last byte to leak stack data when pushed over the network.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces the `lowpan_iphc_mcast_ctx_addr_compress` function which contains the vulnerability. Specifically, `u8 data[6];` is declared uninitialized on the stack. The first `memcpy(data, &ipaddr->s6_addr[1], 2)` writes 2 bytes to `data[0]` and `data[1]`. The second `memcpy(&data[1], &ipaddr->s6_addr[11], 4)` starts at index 1 instead of 2, overwriting `data[1]` and writing up to `data[4]`. This leaves `data[5]` uninitialized, which is then leaked over the network via `lowpan_push_hc_data(hc_ptr, data, 6)`.
